title: Help from Sissle's band members
summary: Ladnier and Bechet helped teach English; dress inspections.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Right. And then you were playing with Nevil Cecil, when Tony Lattner and Sidney Bechet --
What was Lattner like? Did you relate

He was a -- me, I was lucky. (Unintelligible), and they were all looking after me. They were able to teach me English and see that I do the right things, and that I'm happy and everything. They used to tell me, don't get discouraged about nothing. They'd show me what to play here, how to play here, what to do here, you know what I mean? Everything.
I had plenty of help. And Sidney Bechet, too. He was a good man.

He had that kind of problem. (Unintelligible), I don't know. They took me, and there was many personalities in that band. There was -- (unintelligible) was in there, Sidney was in there, (unintelligible) was there. So there was a whole lot of personalities in that band. And Cole was there, Nat King Cole's brother.
What was he called? Junior Cole, was it?

I don't know what they used to call -- he used to play bass, and they used to -- because he had bad feet (unintelligible). We used to use a red tail with a white shirt with a high white collar, with a white bow tie in (unintelligible) band. He used to pass inspection before

If the patent leather shoes ain't shined the way they was supposed to be you don't go on the bandstand, or the (unintelligible) clean like it's supposed to be. And sometimes you go back over there and this guy, he'd take his shoe off.
